title: Beyond the Surface: Measuring Self-Preference in LLM Judgments
main_problem: Existing measures of self-preference in LLM judges conflate bias with differences in response quality.
evaluation_method: The DBG score compares the judge model's scores for its own responses with corresponding gold judgments intended to proxy true response quality.
notes: The abstract reports experiments across LLM versions, sizes, and reasoning abilities, and examines response style and post-training data. It does not explicitly identify the judge models or state whether gold judgments were produced by humans.

title: Direct Judgement Preference Optimization
main_problem: Existing LLM-as-judges are trained with supervised finetuning on small datasets and limited evaluation tasks, which restricts their generalization; the study addresses how to train stronger, more generalized foundational judge models.
judge_model: 8B-, 12B-, and 70B-parameter judge models trained with DPO; GPT-4o is used as a comparison model.
task_or_domain: Evaluating and critiquing large language model responses through pairwise judgement, single-response rating, and classification tasks.
evaluation_method: Evaluation on 13 benchmarks: 7 pairwise, 4 single-rating, and 2 classification benchmarks, using aggregate performance and analysis of critique factuality and actionability.
limitations: The abstract identifies limited data scale and task coverage as limitations of existing judge models; limitations of the proposed models are not stated.
notes: The abstract reports broad benchmark evaluation and improved generalization, but does not specify human evaluation, bias or robustness testing, or multilingual evaluation.

title: From Generation to Judgment: Opportunities and Challenges of LLM -as-a-judge
main_problem: To survey and organize the use of large language models as judges for scoring, ranking, and selection in machine learning evaluation, while identifying challenges and opportunities.
task_or_domain: LLM-based judgment and assessment across various machine learning evaluation scenarios, especially open-ended and dynamic scenarios.
evaluation_method: Introduces a taxonomy covering what to judge, how to judge, and how to benchmark; specific evaluator-quality assessment methods are unclear.
future_work: Highlights promising future directions for the emerging LLM-as-a-judge area, without specifying them in the abstract.
notes: This is presented as a comprehensive survey rather than a study of a specifically named judge model or a single empirical evaluation setting.

title: Arena-lite: Efficient and Reliable Large Language Model Evaluation via Tournament-Based Direct Comparisons
main_problem: Baseline-mediated LLM evaluation can be less reliable than direct system-to-system comparison and may require many comparisons.
task_or_domain: LLM-based system evaluation and model selection
evaluation_method: Arena-Lite is assessed through controlled stochastic modeling and empirical validation with a real LLM judge, focusing on ranking reliability and the number of comparisons required.
notes: The abstract indicates evaluation under smaller datasets and weaker judges, which provides limited evidence of robustness, but it does not specify particular robustness or bias tests. The judge model and any human evaluation comparison are not identified.

title: Are Checklists Really Useful for Automatic Evaluation of Generative Tasks?
main_problem: Determining whether automatically generated checklists improve LLM-based automatic evaluation of generative tasks, and whether they should be used universally or selectively.
task_or_domain: Automatic evaluation of generative tasks using pairwise comparison and direct scoring.
evaluation_method: Checklist-based evaluators are assessed by comparing their performance with human evaluations and by measuring correlations between checklist items and human scores across six checklist-generation methods and eight model sizes.
limitations: The benefits of checklists are less consistent for direct scoring, and some checklist items show low correlation with human scores.
future_work: More clearly define objective evaluation criteria to guide both human and automatic evaluations.
notes: The abstract does not name the evaluator models or report explicit fairness, demographic-bias, or multilingual analyses. Evaluation across model sizes provides some variation for testing consistency, but robustness is not explicitly framed as a dedicated test.

title: Analyzing Uncertainty of LLM -as-a-Judge: Interval Evaluations with Conformal Prediction
main_problem: The uncertainty and reliability of LLM-based evaluation scores are underexplored, limiting the deployment of LLM-as-a-judge systems.
task_or_domain: Natural language generation evaluation with discrete rating tasks.
evaluation_method: Conformal prediction is used to construct prediction intervals for LLM-based scores, with evaluation of interval coverage, interval midpoint scoring, and judge reprompting.
notes: The abstract claims valid prediction intervals with coverage guarantees and describes the midpoint as a low-bias alternative, but it does not specify the judge model, datasets, human evaluation comparison, robustness settings, or languages.

title: Meta-Rewarding Language Models: Self-Improving Alignment with LLM -as-a-Meta-Judge
main_problem: Existing self-rewarding methods improve model responses but not judgment capabilities, leading to rapid saturation during iterative training.
judge_model: Llama-3-8B-Instruct is explicitly named as the improved model; the specific external judge/evaluator models are not stated.
task_or_domain: LLM alignment, instruction following, and self-evaluation of model judgments.
evaluation_method: Performance is assessed using win rates on AlpacaEval 2 and Arena-Hard before and after meta-rewarding.
limitations: Existing self-rewarding approaches are described as rapidly saturating during iterative training; no further limitation of the proposed approach is stated.
notes: The abstract reports unsupervised self-judging and improvements in benchmark win rates, but does not specify whether those evaluations involve human judgments, particular evaluator models, bias analyses, robustness tests, or multiple languages.

title: Self-Augmented Preference Alignment for Sycophancy Reduction in LLM s
main_problem: Reducing sycophantic behavior in LLMs, particularly the tendency to favor user expectations over truthful responses, and assessing how human-feedback alignment affects sycophancy.
task_or_domain: Sycophancy assessment and reduction in open-source language models across multiple tasks.
evaluation_method: The study directly compares models aligned with human feedback to models not aligned with human feedback, using the Sycophancy Answer Assessment dataset and Self-Augmented Preference Alignment to evaluate assessment ability and sycophancy reduction.
notes: The abstract does not name a judge or evaluator model. Human feedback is central to the comparison, but the abstract does not explicitly report comparison with human evaluation scores or judgments.

title: Improve LLM -as-a-Judge Ability as a General Ability
main_problem: Developing an accurate and data-efficient LLM-as-a-Judge model with judging ability treated as a general capability.
task_or_domain: Evaluation of LLM responses and provision of reward signals for RLHF across diverse scenarios.
evaluation_method: Performance is evaluated on RewardBench, with additional validation through deployment for reward-signal provision in a real-world RLHF scenario.
future_work: The authors state that they will open-source the model weights and training data.
notes: The abstract reports improved general capabilities and data efficiency, but does not specify the judge model, human-evaluation protocol, bias or robustness tests, or multilingual settings.

title: Towards Optimal Evaluation Efficiency for Large Language Models
main_problem: Reducing the data-annotation and computational costs of LLM evaluation while preserving evaluation reliability and benchmark semantic information.
task_or_domain: Efficient evaluation of LLMs using selected subsets of questions from large-scale benchmarks.
evaluation_method: The selected-subset approach is evaluated by score reliability or accuracy using the L2 norm, compared with clustering-based methods, and by semantic retention using Wasserstein distance.
notes: The abstract describes optimization-based question subset selection, including optimal random sampling and simulated annealing, but does not name a judge model or provide details about human evaluation, bias, robustness, or language coverage.

title: C heck E val: A reliable LLM -as-a-Judge framework for evaluating text generation using checklists
main_problem: Inconsistent and variable ratings across LLM evaluators when judging text generation.
evaluation_method: A checklist-based framework using decomposed binary questions is assessed through correlation with human judgments, agreement across 12 evaluator models, and score variance across multiple datasets.
notes: The abstract mentions 12 evaluator models but does not name them. Multiple evaluator models and datasets are reported, but explicit bias, robustness, or multilinguality analyses are not described.

title: Multi-perspective Analysis of Large Language Model Domain Specialization: An Experiment in Accounting Audit Procedures Generation
main_problem: Investigating how fine-tuning, in-context learning, and their combination affect the characteristics of generated text in domain-specialized LLMs.
task_or_domain: Accounting Audit Procedures Generation (AAPG), requiring specialized accounting knowledge.
evaluation_method: An experimental comparison of output characteristics across models using fine-tuning, in-context learning, and combined approaches; specific evaluation procedures are not stated.
notes: The abstract reports consistent differences in output characteristics but does not identify an evaluator model, human assessment, or specific evaluation criteria.

title: Debatable Intelligence: Benchmarking LLM Judges via Debate Speech Evaluation
main_problem: Assessing how well LLMs act as judges of debate speeches and identifying differences between LLM and human judgment behavior.
task_or_domain: Debate speech evaluation, including argument strength and relevance, coherence and organization, and style and tone.
evaluation_method: LLM judgments are evaluated against judgments from humans using a dataset of over 600 annotated debate speeches, with analysis of agreement and overall judgment behavior.
notes: The abstract names only state-of-the-art/frontier LLMs without specifying models. It does not explicitly describe bias, robustness, or multilingual tests.

title: Beyond the Score: Uncertainty-Calibrated LLM s for Automated Essay Assessment
main_problem: Lack of confidence measures and explanations in automated essay scoring, limiting real-world and high-stakes adoption.
task_or_domain: Automated Essay Scoring (AES) across the ASAP, TOEFL11, and Cambridge-FCE corpora.
evaluation_method: Conformal prediction calibrated at a 90% risk level, evaluated using coverage guarantees and UAcc, which rewards correctness and concise prediction sets.
limitations: Real-world adoption, especially in high-stakes examinations, remains limited; no further study limitations are explicitly stated.
future_work: Scaling the approach and conducting broader user studies.
notes: The named LLMs are fine-tuned essay-scoring models rather than explicitly described as LLM judges. The abstract mentions near-human agreement as background but does not report a direct human comparison in this study. Conformal coverage and compact prediction sets provide evidence about uncertainty reliability, but bias, multilinguality, and broader robustness are not explicitly evaluated.

title: MR . Judge: Multimodal Reasoner as a Judge
main_problem: How to equip general-purpose multimodal large language model judges with stronger reasoning capabilities for evaluating responses.
judge_model: MR. Judge, including MR. Judge-7B; the specific underlying MLLM judge architecture is not otherwise named.
task_or_domain: Multimodal response evaluation for RLHF and inference-time scaling, evaluated on VL-RewardBench and MM-Vet.
evaluation_method: Judge quality is assessed by benchmark performance, including comparison with GPT-4o on VL-RewardBench and improvements on MM-Vet during inference-time scaling.
limitations: The abstract identifies a lack of questions with scored responses for training and automatic annotation; no other explicit limitations are stated.
notes: The method reframes judging as deliberate reasoning followed by multiple-choice selection and uses reverse response candidate synthesis plus text-based reasoning distillation. The abstract does not specify human evaluation, bias or robustness tests, or multilingual coverage.

title: Co-Eval: Augmenting LLM -based Evaluation with Machine Metrics
main_problem: LLM-based evaluators can exhibit bias and misalignment, especially on domain-specific tasks, due to limited functional understanding and knowledge gaps.
task_or_domain: Natural language generation tasks, including general and domain-specific tasks.
evaluation_method: Evaluates the relationship between evaluator familiarity and performance, measures reduction in self-preference bias, and assesses alignment with human preferences using Spearman correlation.
limitations: LLM-based evaluations may suffer from biases, misalignment, limited functional understanding, and knowledge gaps, particularly in domain-specific tasks.
notes: No specific judge model, machine metrics, or domain-specific application is named in the abstract.

title: Model Consistency as a Cheap yet Predictive Proxy for LLM Elo Scores
main_problem: Developing a cheap, independent proxy for evaluating LLM performance without expensive human comparisons.
task_or_domain: LLM contests or pairwise matchups in which an evaluator selects the better model output.
evaluation_method: Assessing the correlation between an LLM judge's consistency in selecting the best model in matchups and that model's human-produced Elo score; the reported correlation is 91%.
notes: The abstract describes consistency as a proxy for human-based Elo scores, but does not specify the judge model, datasets, languages, or dedicated bias and robustness analyses.

title: Can Large Language Models Outperform Non-Experts in Poetry Evaluation? A Comparative Study Using the Consensual Assessment Technique
main_problem: Whether LLMs can reliably evaluate poetry and outperform non-expert human judges using a comparative assessment framework.
evaluation_method: LLM rankings were compared with a ground truth based on publication venue using Spearman’s Rank Correlation; inter-rater reliability was also assessed.
notes: The study uses forced-choice ranking in small randomized batches and reports high inter-rater reliability, but the abstract does not describe explicit bias, multilingual, or cross-condition robustness tests.
